exampleAnswers.title: Finding a Unit Vector Parallel to a Given Vector

question.text: The vector $\mathbf{m}$ has magnitude $\dfrac 7 2.$ Find a unit vector that is parallel to $\mathbf{m}.$
question.explanation: To obtain the unit vector that is parallel to $\mathbf{m}$, we divide $\mathbf{m}$ by its length: \[ \mathbf{u}=\dfrac{\mathbf{m}}{|\,\mathbf{m}\,|} = \dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac 7 2\right)}\mathbf{m}= \dfrac 2 7\mathbf{m} \]

exampleAnswers.title: Finding a Unit Vector Parallel to a Given Vector in a Diagram

question.text:
Consider the picture above. Find a unit vector $\mathbf{u}$ that is parallel to $\mathbf{p}+\mathbf{q}$ and has the same direction as $\mathbf p + \mathbf q.$

Type $p$ and $q$ to represent the vectors $\mathbf p$ and $\mathbf q,$ respectively.
question.explanation:
First, we have to find $\mathbf{p+q}.$ According to the triangle law of addition, the resultant $\mathbf{p}+\mathbf{q}$ goes from the tail of $\mathbf{p}$ to the head of $\mathbf{q}\mathbin{:}$

In $\bigtriangleup AHB$, we have $\angle AHB = 90^\circ$, $AH=2$ and $BH=3.$ So, the Pythagorean theorem gives \begin{align*} |\mathbf{p}+\mathbf{q}| &= AB \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{AH^2+BH^2} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{(2)^2 + (3)^2} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{4+9} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{13}. \end{align*}

Hence, the magnitude of $\mathbf{p}+\mathbf{q}$ is $\sqrt{13}.$ Consequently, the unit vector is \begin{align*} \mathbf{u} &= \dfrac{1}{|\mathbf{p}+\mathbf{q}|} \cdot (\mathbf{p}+\mathbf{q}) \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{13}}(\mathbf{p}+\mathbf{q})}. \end{align*}

example.title: Finding a Unit Vector Parallel to a Given Vector in a Diagram

question.text: Consider the picture above. Which of the following is a unit vector that is parallel to $\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{r}?$
question.explanation:
First, we have to find $\mathbf{q+r}.$ According to the triangle law of addition, the resultant $\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{r}$ goes from the tail of $\mathbf{q}$ to the head of $\mathbf{r}\mathbin{:}$

In $\bigtriangleup AHB$, we have $\angle AHB = 90^\circ$, $AH=1.5=\dfrac32$ and $BH=4.$ So, the Pythagorean theorem gives

\begin{align*} |\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{r}| &= AB \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{AH^2+BH^2} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^2+4^2} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\sqrt{73}}{2}. \end{align*}

Hence, the magnitude of $\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{r}$ is $\dfrac{\sqrt{73}}{2}.$ Consequently, the unit vector is \begin{align*} \mathbf{u} &= \dfrac{1}{|\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{r}|} \cdot (\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{r}) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2(\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{r})}{\sqrt{73}}. \end{align*}

question.text: Consider the picture shown above. Which of the following is a unit vector that is parallel to $\mathbf{p}?$
question.explanation:
In $\bigtriangleup AHB$, we have $\angle AHB = 90^\circ$, $AH=2$ and $BH=5.$ So, the Pythagorean theorem gives

\begin{align*} AB &= \sqrt{AH^2+BH^2} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{2^2+5^2} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{4+25} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{29}. \end{align*}

Hence, the magnitude of $\mathbf{p}$ is $\sqrt{29}.$ Consequently, the unit vector is \begin{align*} \mathbf{u} &= \dfrac{1}{|\,\mathbf{p}\,|} \cdot \mathbf{p} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{29}}\mathbf{p}. \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Finding a Unit Vector Parallel to a Vector Sum

question.text: The vector $\mathbf{a}$ is directed due north-east and $|\,\mathbf{a}\,|=7$, while the vector $\mathbf{b}$ is directed due north-west and $|\,\mathbf{b}\,|=7.$ Which of the following is a unit vector that is parallel to $\mathbf{a+b}?$
question.explanation:
First, we have to find $\mathbf{a+b}.$ According to the triangle law of addition, the resultant $\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}$ goes from the tail of $\mathbf{a}$ to the head of $\mathbf{b}\mathbin{:}$

To find the unit vector corresponding to $\mathbf{a+b},$ we have to divide by the magnitude: \[ \begin{align*} \mathbf{u} &= \dfrac {\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}}{\left|\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}\right|} \end{align*} \]

To find the magnitude, first notice that we obtain a right triangle. So, we can use the Pythagorean theorem: \[ \begin{align*} {|\mathbf{a+b}|}^2 &={|\mathbf{a}|}^2+{|\mathbf{b}|}^2 \\[3pt] &={7}^2+{7}^2 \\[3pt] &=98 \end{align*} \]

Therefore, the magnitude is \[ |\mathbf{a+b}|=\sqrt{98}=7\sqrt{2}, \] and the corresponding unit vector is \[ \begin{align*} \mathbf{u} &= \dfrac {\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}}{\left|\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}\right|} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{7\sqrt{2}}\left(\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}\right). \end{align*} \]

question.explanation:
First, we have to find $\mathbf{a+b}.$ According to the triangle law of addition, the resultant $\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}$ goes from the tail of $\mathbf{a}$ to the head of $\mathbf{b}\mathbin{:}$

To find the unit vector corresponding to $\mathbf{a+b},$ we have to divide by the magnitude: \[ \begin{align*} \mathbf{u} &= \dfrac {\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}}{\left|\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}\right|} \end{align*} \]

To find the magnitude, first notice that we obtain a right triangle. So, we can use the Pythagorean theorem: \[ \begin{align*} {|\mathbf{a+b}|}^2 &={|\mathbf{a}|}^2+{|\mathbf{b}|}^2 \\[3pt] &={5}^2+{12}^2 \\[3pt] &=169 \end{align*} \]

Therefore, the magnitude is \[ |\mathbf{a+b}|=\sqrt{169}=13, \] and the corresponding unit vector is \[ \begin{align*} \mathbf{u} &= \dfrac {\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}}{\left|\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}\right|} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{13}\left(\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}\right). \end{align*} \]

example.title: Finding a Unit Vector Parallel to a Vector Sum

question.text:
The vector $\mathbf{a}$ is directed horizontally to the right and has magnitude $\sqrt{3}$, while the vector $\mathbf{b}$ is directed vertically up and has magnitude $\sqrt{6}.$ Find a unit vector $\mathbf{u}$ that is parallel to $\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}$ and has the same direction as $\mathbf a + \mathbf b.$

Type $a$ and $b$ to represent the vectors $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b,$ respectively.
question.explanation:
First, we have to find $\mathbf{a+b}.$ According to the triangle law of addition, the resultant $\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}$ goes from the tail of $\mathbf{a}$ to the head of $\mathbf{b}\mathbin{:}$

To find the unit vector corresponding to $\mathbf{a+b},$ we have to divide by the magnitude: \begin{align*} \mathbf{u} &= \dfrac {\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}}{\left|\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}\right|} \end{align*}

To find the magnitude, first notice that we obtain a right triangle. So, we can use the Pythagorean theorem: \begin{align*} {|\mathbf{a+b}|}^2 &={|\mathbf{a}|}^2+{|\mathbf{b}|}^2 \\[5pt] &=\left(\sqrt{3}\right)^2+\left(\sqrt{6}\right)^2 \\[5pt] &=3+6 \\[3pt] &=9 \end{align*}

Therefore, the magnitude is \[ |\mathbf{a+b}|=\sqrt{9}=3, \] and the corresponding unit vector is \begin{align*} \mathbf{u} &= \dfrac {\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}}{\left|\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}\right|} \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{1}{3}\left(\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}\right)}. \end{align*}
